action: Quantum Systems operators: follow the company's and your authority's guidance; the company says there is no risk in operating its systems.
exec: A cyberattack on a defence supplier led its military customer to ground equipment as a precaution, showing supplier risk reaching operations.
plain: German drone maker Quantum Systems confirmed a cyberattack from October. The German military grounded its drones as a precaution; on 13 November the company said they were flying again.
summary: Quantum Systems confirmed an active cyberattack by "hostile actors", noticed in October, that it says its teams contained. Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, as relayed by Security Affairs and Euronews, report attackers may have used a malicious update and that the German military stopped using its drones. On 13 November the company told Reuters the Bundeswehr drones were flying again. No attacker is named.
title: German military grounds Quantum Systems drones after cyberattack on the maker

validation.note: Security Affairs (Nov 16) and Euronews (Nov 13) both relay the company statement and Spiegel/FT reporting. The malicious update is reported as possible, not confirmed. Reuters (via TimesLIVE, read 21 Nov): company says the Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground systems; the German military had no immediate comment.

date_note: Company confirmed the attack publicly on November 12-13 (Euronews, November 13); Security Affairs covered it on November 16.

review.note: Checked against Security Affairs and Euronews (Spiegel/FT relay). Date moved from Nov 16 to Nov 13 (company went public); update wording made 'reported/possible'; Euronews added as second publisher; plain no longer states the update as fact. Correction file added.
